$comment: Accepted-for-this-release defects. A waiver here does NOT hide a failure:
the rule still runs, still reports FAIL, and meets_the_bar still prints it —
it just stops that one rule blocking an unrelated release. This exists so a
known defect in one app cannot hold every other app's work hostage, which is
what happens when shared-file changes pull every app into the push range.
- Every entry names ONE app and ONE rule. No wildcards, no 'all'.
- Every entry states why it is accepted and what will fix it.
- `since` is the date it was first accepted. An entry that keeps being
renewed is a decision to look at, not a fact of life.
- lg-shipped is NOT waivable. Ship proof is the one thing a release cannot
take on credit; enforced in code, not by convention.
